answer: An AI agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with collateral-backed identity and random audits. Before voting, each agent locks a bond tied to a unique attestation; the registry records which key owns it, and stakes cannot be shared. Validators broadcast an echo challenge and demand a signed reply from every identity, so one comet node posing as many agents must hold many keys. Audits check whether replies ripple from a single operator; caught clones forfeit every bond. A majority attacker must fund N separate stakes and risks losing all N, so cost grows linearly, not free.
